title: Working with Service Bus Queues
description: Create and use Service Bus queues to reliably send and receive messages in order.

data.text: A Service Bus queue stores messages until a receiver is ready to process them. You can configure settings such as message time-to-live (TTL), maximum queue size, and whether duplicate detection is enabled.

data.title: Create a Service Bus Queue (Azure CLI)
data.content: Create a queue named orders inside your namespace:
data.code:
az servicebus queue create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --namespace-name myNamespace \
  --name orders \
  --max-size-in-megabytes 1024 \
  --default-message-time-to-live P14D \
  --duplicate-detection-history-time-window PT10M

data.text: To send a message, your application creates a ServiceBusClient, builds a ServiceBusMessage, and sends it using the sender. Messages can be plain text, JSON, or binary data.

data.title: Send a Message (JavaScript/TypeScript)

data.text: Receivers can use the peek-lock mode, which locks a message for a period while the receiver processes it. If processing succeeds, the receiver completes the message. If it fails, the message can be abandoned so another receiver can try.

data.title: Receive and Process Messages (JavaScript/TypeScript)
data.content: Receive messages from a queue using a processor:

terms.definition: A receive mode where the broker locks a message so no other receiver can process it simultaneously.
Tell Service Bus that a message was processed successfully and remove it from the queue.
Release the lock on a message so it becomes available again for another receiver.
Time-to-live: how long a message stays in the queue before it expires.

data.caption: Queue message lifecycle
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Producer sends message] --> B[Message stored in queue]
    B --> C{Receiver available?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Message locked and delivered]
    D --> E{Processing succeeded?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Complete: message removed]
    E -->|No| G[Abandon: lock released]
    G --> B
    C -->|No| B

data.title: Configure a Queue for E-Commerce Orders
data.description: Design the right queue settings for an order-processing system that must guarantee ordered processing and no message loss.
steps: Set the max-size-in-megabytes to support 100,000 pending orders (approximately 1 KB each).
Enable duplicate detection with a 5-minute window.
Set a TTL so messages expire after 7 days if not processed.
data.expectedOutcome: A queue configured with 1024 MB max size, duplicate-detection-history-time-window PT5M, default-message-time-to-live P7D, and enable-partitioning true.
